answer: Picture each agent as a comet: to shine it must burn real fuel. In PoA every identity pays per-epoch proof-of-work and must pen an original, peer-graded text with its own quill — duplicates are rejected on-ledger. A sybil swarm therefore pays N times the compute and must forge N distinct coherent essays, while the nectar of rewards per identity stays capped. Cost scales linearly with fakes; profit doesn't, so the attack starves itself.
